## Load and Cleaning Data

In this section, describe the source of the data, write a basic data dictionary for data you are working with, and discuss any caveats or issues you discovered working with this data. 

```{r}
# Loading required datasets and cleaning them 
age_pop <- read_csv("data/population-by-age.csv") |> 
  clean_names()

private_enrollment <- read_csv("data/private-enrollment-by-grade.csv") |> 
  clean_names() |> 
# Renaming so that we can join later 
  rename(state_abbr = "state") |> 
  rename(private_enrollment = "enrollment")

public_enrollment <- read.csv("data/public-enrollment-by-grade.csv") |> 
  clean_names() |> 
# Renaming so that we can join later 
  rename(state_abbr = "st") |> 
  rename(public_enrollment = "enrollment")

# Creating a new combined dataset to analyze enrollment rates later 
school_story <- public_enrollment |> 
  left_join(private_enrollment, join_by(fips, sch_year, grade, state_abbr)) |> 
# Filtering down to the states that the AP analyzed 
  filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12)) |> 
  select(-data_source)



```

## Sentences to Engineer
In this notebook, we are reverse engineering five sentences from the story.

### Sentence 1

* **Sentence text**: “The population of school-age kids in the states we studied fell by about 183,000, according to census estimates.” 

* **Analysis summary**: Our results confirmed the AP's claim stating that the population of school-age kids in the 22 states studied fell by about 183,000. We found this number by finding the difference between the provided age and population data from July 2020 to the age and population data we have from July 2021.

```{r}

# Creating new dataset to focus on estimated school-age population in 2020 in the respective jurisdiction 
age_2020_pop <- age_pop |> 
# Creating new columns based on the est_date column
  mutate(year = year(est_date), month = month(est_date)) |> 
# Filtering down to April 2020 to match the AP estimated start date for school-age population
  filter(year == 2020 & month == 4) |>
# Filtering to match the states that the AP examined 
  filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12)) |> 
# Calculating the total school-age population in April 2020 per state 
  group_by(state, fips) |> 
  summarise(total_pop_2020 = sum(population))

# Creating new dataset to focus on estimated school-age population in 2021 in the respective jurisdiction 
age_2021_pop <- age_pop |> 
# Creating new columns based on the est_date column
  mutate(year = year(est_date), month = month(est_date)) |> 
# Filtering down to July 2021 to match the AP estimated start date for school-age population
  filter(year == 2021 & month == 7) |>
# Filtering to match the states that the AP examined 
  filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12)) |> 
# Calculating the total school-age population in July 2021 per state 
  group_by(state, fips) |> 
  summarise(total_pop_2021 = sum(population))

# Creating official dataset for sentence #1 analysis 
combo_age_year <- age_2021_pop |> 
  left_join(age_2020_pop, join_by(state)) |> 
# Calculating the school-age population difference between 2020-2021 per state 
  mutate(difference = total_pop_2021 - total_pop_2020) |> 
# Finding the overall difference (the number that the AP got that is shown in the Missing Kids Summary spreadsheet)
  summarise(total_difference = sum(difference))
  
```

### Sentence 2

* **Sentence text**: “Those states saw private-school enrollment grow by over 100,000 students." 
* **Analysis summary**: Our results confirmed the AP’s claim that private school enrollment in the 22 states studied grew by over 100,000 students. The AP article also states that private school enrollment grew by “about 103,000 students.” We found this number by comparing total private school enrollment in the 22 states studied between the 2019-2020 and the 2021-2022 school years. This gives us a difference of 102,847 which explains both sentences where this number is referenced in the AP’s story. 

```{r}

private_change <- private_enrollment |> 
  filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12)) |> 
  filter(str_detect(grade, "k_12_total")) |> 
  filter(sch_year == "2019-2020" | sch_year == "2021-2022") |> 
  group_by(sch_year) |> 
  summarise(total_enrollment = sum(private_enrollment)) 

# Calculated difference is: 102,847 (exact same as the AP stat)
  
```

### Sentence 3

* **Sentence text**: "In the 21 states where data was available, enrollment fell by about 700,000 students between the 2019-2020 and 2021-2022 school years." 

* **Analysis summary**:  To find this change, we first created a filter from the available public school enrollment data, searching for the total enrollment in K-12 schools. The filter separated enrollment in the 2019-20 and 2021-22 academic years. We were then able to subtract the total enrollment we previously calculated from the sum of our public school enrollment data, and got 704,593, which is the number that the AP presented.

```{r}

public_change <- public_enrollment |> 
  filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12)) |> 
  filter(str_detect(grade, "k_12_total")) |> 
  filter(sch_year == "2019-2020" | sch_year == "2021-2022") |> 
  group_by(sch_year) |> 
  summarise(total_enrollment = sum(public_enrollment)) 

# Calculated difference is : -704,593 (exact same as the AP stat)

```

### Sentence 4

* **Sentence text**: "An analysis by The Associated Press, Stanford University’s Big Local News project and Stanford education professor Thomas Dee found an estimated 230,000 students in 21 states whose absences could not be accounted for. These students didn’t move out of state, and they didn’t sign up for private school or home-school, according to publicly available data.”

* **Analysis summary**: Here, we are finding the 230,000 unaccounted for students the AP found. We then used the available enrollment changes data to find homeschool enrollment growing by over 180,000, which is mentioned in the article. Subtracting the enrollment changes from homeschool, private, and public while also accounting for the drop in population left us with 234,213, which is the number of unaccounted students mentioned in the article.

```{r}

enrollment_changes <- read_csv("data/enrollment_changes.csv") |> 
  clean_names()

homeschool_enrollment <- enrollment_changes |> 
  filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12)) |> 
  filter(enrollment_type == "Homeschool enrollment") |>
  select(fips, state_abbrev, total_change) |>
  summarise(total_enrollment = sum(total_change, na.rm = TRUE)) 

# Calculated difference is : 184,047 (exact same as the AP stat)

# Calculated residual : (-704,593 + 102,847 + 184,047) - -183,486 = -234,213 (exact same stat for the AP number)

```

### Sentence 5

* **Sentence text**: “States where kindergarten is optional were more likely to have larger numbers of unaccounted-for students, suggesting the missing also include many young learners kept home instead of starting school.”

* **Analysis summary**: [Write up two to three sentences describing the results of your analysis.  Were you able to confirm the finding? If not, why not?]

```{r}

private_2020_change <- private_enrollment |> 
  filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12)) |> 
  filter(str_detect(grade, "k_12_total")) |> 
  filter(sch_year == "2019-2020") |> 
  rename(year_one = "sch_year") |> 
  rename(enroll_2020 = "private_enrollment")

private_2022_change <- private_enrollment |> 
  filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12)) |> 
  filter(str_detect(grade, "k_12_total")) |> 
  filter(sch_year == "2021-2022") |> 
  rename(year_two = "sch_year") |> 
  rename(enroll_2022 = "private_enrollment")

pri_table <- private_2020_change |> 
  left_join(private_2022_change, join_by(fips, grade, state_abbr)) |> 
  mutate(total_pri_change = enroll_2022 - enroll_2020) |> 
  select(fips, state_abbr, total_pri_change)


homeschool_table <- enrollment_changes |> 
  filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12)) |> 
  filter(enrollment_type == "Homeschool enrollment") |>
  rename(total_home_change = total_change) |>
  rename(state_abbr = "state_abbrev") |>
  select(fips, state_abbr, total_home_change) 


public_2020_change <- public_enrollment |> 
  filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12)) |> 
  filter(str_detect(grade, "k_12_total")) |> 
  filter(sch_year == "2019-2020") |> 
  rename(year_one = "sch_year") |> 
  rename(enroll_2020 = "public_enrollment")

public_2022_change <- public_enrollment |> 
  filter(fips %in% c(6, 36, 22, 37, 53, 8, 13, 27, 55, 33, 25, 30, 10, 38, 11, 46, 45, 31, 44, 47, 42, 12)) |> 
  filter(str_detect(grade, "k_12_total")) |> 
  filter(sch_year == "2021-2022") |> 
  rename(year_two = "sch_year") |> 
  rename(enroll_2022 = "public_enrollment")

pub_table <- public_2020_change |> 
  left_join(public_2022_change, join_by(fips, grade, state_abbr)) |> 
  mutate(total_pub_change = enroll_2022 - enroll_2020) |> 
  select(fips, state_abbr, total_pub_change)

age_group <- age_2021_pop |> 
  left_join(age_2020_pop, join_by(state, fips)) |> 
  mutate(difference = total_pop_2021 - total_pop_2020) |>
  select(-total_pop_2021, -total_pop_2020)

summary_file <- read_csv("data/missing_kids_summary.csv") |> 
  clean_names() |> 
  select(fips, kindergarten_required)

missing_kids <- pri_table |> 
  left_join(pub_table, join_by(fips, state_abbr)) |> 
  left_join(homeschool_table, join_by(fips, state_abbr)) |> 
  left_join(age_group, join_by(fips)) |>
  left_join(summary_file, join_by(fips)) |>
  select(-state) |> 
  mutate(residual = (total_pri_change + total_pub_change + total_home_change) - difference)
  
```
